==Biography==
Revolta started playing competitively in late 2012 for vVv Gaming Brazil. In the beginning of 2013, he joined Insight eSports, coming out of retirement. 

===2014 Season===
For the first half of the 2024 season, [[Revolta]] played in the jungle for [[CNB e-Sports Club]]. In August, he rejoined [[Keyd Stars]]. On November 6, Revolta was moved to a substitute position within the [[Keyd Stars]] roster, as the result of a decision to give him time to take care of personal issues away from the team. Though he was still contracted to the team, he was given the option to play for other teams on a loan.<ref>[http://www.facebook.com/keydteam/posts/732282933513227 Keyd's Facebook] ''facebook.com''</ref>
On November 24, Revolta left Keyd Stars.<ref>[http://www.facebook.com/revolta.LoL/posts/691796937586378 Revolta's Facebook Post] ''facebook.com''</ref> Shortly after, he joined [[INTZ e-Sports]].<ref>[http://www.facebook.com/revolta.LoL/photos/696014423831296 Revolta's Facebook post] ''facebook.com''</ref>

===2015 Season===
In the first split of 2015, '''Revolta''' played as the jungler for [[INTZ e-Sports]] in the CBLOL. The team achieved significant success, culminating in a victory over [[Keyd Stars]] in the [[CBLOL 2015 Split 1 Playoffs|CBLOL 2015 Split 1 finals]], which secured them a spot at the [[IWCI 2015|International Wildcard Invitational]] (IWCI). Despite their strong performance domestically, '''INTZ''' did not advance to the [[MSI 2015|Mid-Season Invitational]], as they were defeated in the IWCI by [[Beşiktaş Esports]]. Following the first split, Revolta made a notable and very criticized move by joining [[Keyd Stars]] for the second split of the year. However, this transition did not yield the desired results, as Keyd Stars were eliminated by [[g3nerationX|g3x]] in the playoffs, preventing them from reaching the finals. In the final moments of the year, Revolta rejoined '''INTZ'''.

===2016 Season===
In 2016 he was part of the lineup that is often referred as the Exodia of CBLOL: [[Yang (Felipe Zhao)|Yang]], [[Revolta]], [[tockers]], [[micaO]] and [[Jockster]], led by [[Peter Dun]] and [[Abaxial]]. The team managed to never lose a series that they played on Brazilian soil. They played at [[CBLOL 2016 Split 1]] and consequently won [[CBLOL 2016 Split 1 Playoffs]] after beating [[Keyd Stars]] for 3x0 in the Grand Finals. With the win, they classified [[INTZ]] to the [[2016 International Wildcard Invitational]], where they managed to achieve 3rd place among other Wildcards regions.
In the [[CBLOL 2016 Split 2|second split]], they found theyselves in a rivalry against [[CNB e-Sports Club]] until they beated them by 3-1 in the [[CBLOL 2016 Split 2 Playoffs|finals]]. In the [[IWCQ 2016]], they managed to classify to [[Worlds 2016]], where they made history by being the only Brazilian team to defeat an Asian team from a Major league by defeating [[EDward Gaming]], despite not qualifying for the main stage of the tournament.<ref>[https://www.espn.com.br/esports/artigo/_/id/5732003/adeus-exodia-o-fim-e-o-legado-do-quinteto-mais-vitorioso-do-cblol Adeus, Exodia: o fim e o legado do quinteto mais vitorioso do CBLoL] ''espn.com.br''</ref> In the end of 2016, '''Revolta''' decided to leave '''INTZ''' and rejoined [[Keyd Stars]] once again.

===2017 Season=== 
With [[Revolta]]'s return to Keyd Stars, the team showed strong performances, but despite the individual talent, they fell short of the title. Revolta and his team reached the [[CBLOL 2017 Split 1 Playoffs]], but were defeated by [[RED Canids]] in the finals. Despite this setback, the year remained relatively positive, as INTZ secured a spot in the [[Rift Rivals 2017 LLN-CLS-CBLOL|Rift Rivals]] and won. For the second split of the year, they ended up almost being demoted to the [[BRCC 2018 Split 1|BRCC]] after finishing 6th place in the CBLOL 2017 Split 2. Luckily, they won the [[CBLOL 2018 Split 1 Promotion]] after defeating [[Iron Hawks e-Sports]] and weren't demoted.

===2018 Season===  
In 2018, Keyd attempted a revival of INTZ's successful "Exodia" and almost managed to win their first split back together, but finished second in the [[CBLOL 2018 Split 1 Playoffs|CBLOL 2018 Split 1 Finals]] after losing by 3-2 against [[KaBuM! Esports]]. They also secured a spot in the [[Rift Rivals 2018 LLN-CLS-CBLOL|Rift Rivals]] of the same year, and won again. In the Split 2, they lost their coach, [[Abaxial]], who left for [[RED Canids]], and the team fell short despite [[Galfi]]'s efforts in the regular season, in which they finished fifth. In playoffs, they lost to [[CNB e-Sports Club|CNB]] and finished fourth.

===2019 Season===
In 2019, Revolta faced new challenges as he transitioned to [[RED Canids]], aiming to bring his expertise to a team that had been playing in the [[BRCC 2019 Split 1|BRCC]]. With Revolta in the lineup, RED Canids managed to finish both splits in the 1st and 2nd place respectively in Split 1 and 2, but didn't win any titles.

===2020 Season===
As the 2020 season began, Revolta continued with RED Canids, looking to build on the previous year's performances. The team didn't show much improvement, finishing fifth in the regular season of [[BRCC 2020 Split 1]] and not qualifying for the playoffs. 
In May, Revolta signed with [[KaBuM! Esports]], hoping to revitalize his career and help the team reclaim their championship status. They had a solid run, finishing the [[CBLOL 2020 Split 2]] in third place but were knocked out in the semifinals by [[INTZ]]. After about six months with KaBuM, Revolta decided to make a move.

===2021 Season===
Revolta returned to [[INTZ]] for the [[CBLOL 2021 Split 1]], seeking to add to his legacy with the team where he had achieved so much success in the past. However, the team's performance was not up to the expectations, and they finished the split in seventh place. Revolta's final competitive match was during this split, after which he left the team. He never officially retired, but didn't play competitively again after. 
After this split, he focused on streaming and content creation, engaging with fans through various online platforms.

===2022 to 2024 Season===
Between 2022 and 2024, '''Revolta''' remained low in the scene and focused in content creation. In 2024, he was invited by [[Baiano]] to coach [[Ilha das Lendas|a team]] focused on content creation and to climb to the [[CBLOL Academy 2024 Split 1|CBLOL Academy]] through the [[CBLOL Academy 2024 Split 1 Q1]]. The project fell short in the first qualifier, and Revolta eventually left the team, but was invited afterwards to join the [[Ilha das Lendas]] group as a streamer.

General Trivia=
===General Trivia===
* Known for his {{ci|Evelynn}}, {{ci|Jarvan IV}}, {{ci|Lee Sin}} and {{ci|Nocturne}}.
* His favorite champion is {{ci|Twisted Fate}}.
* His laugh is often compared to {{ci|Singed}}'s.
* He also likes to play in the mid lane if possible.
* Featured in Riot's Legends Rising Season 2, along with [[Rekkles]], [[ClearLove]], [[WildTurtle]], [[Smeb]], and [[Chawy]].
* Retired for a short period of time in the end of 2013 but came back to give one more chance to an e-Sports career.
* Considered the best player in the Brazilian scene in 2015.
* Was infamously known for missing smites at crucial moments, being called the "Brazilian [[Saintvicious]]".
* Was criticized by many when he returned to [[Keyd Stars|Keyd]] in 2015, being called a mercenary for leaving INTZ after winning the [[CBLOL 2015 Split 1 Playoffs|CBLOL Summer Split]].
* Portrayed as {{ci|Gragas}} in the CBLoL 2015 official wallpaper.
* He is considered one of the greatests junglers in the history of CBLOL by analysts and journalists. <ref>[https://www.fragster.com/br/3-maiores-junglers-brasil-lol/ LoL: Os 3 maiores junglers do Brasil no League of Legends (Portuguese)] ''fragster.com''</ref> 
* He says that [[Winged]] was the jungler who taught him to play, during Winged's time in [[Keyd Stars]] in 2014.
* His favorite player is [[Clearlove]].
* His top 5 junglers of all time are [[DanDy]], [[Bengi]], [[Clearlove]], [[Karsa]] and [[Ambition]].
* Revolta was approached by [[LOUD]] to work as the team's head coach in 2024, but he turned down the proposals so he could focus on his streams. <ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YSQvNVmSPYg MD3 Podcast Cut - Revolta & Tockers] ''youtube.com''</ref>
* He is one of the few Brazilian players known to have been privately coached by [[Nelson]], along with [[Boal]].<ref>[https://twitter.com/ilhadaslendas/status/1753594194659061783 Ilha das Lendas' Tweet] ''twitter.com''</ref>
